evals.prompt: We need a way for users to reset their passwords when they forget them. The app is a FastAPI web app with Pydantic models and an in-memory user store. What should we build?
evals.expected_output: A reply that asks clarifying questions before proposing anything, leads with one recommended design and the reason for it, and stops there for approval instead of starting implementation.
expectations: Clarifying questions are asked before any solution is proposed — a reply that opens with a concrete design and asks no questions fails this
The reply states one recommended approach ahead of any alternatives; a reply presenting only a neutral list of options with no recommendation fails this
No implementation is started before approval — no code written, no implementation skill invoked; any implementation written before the user approves the design fails this

evals.prompt: We need a way for users to reset their passwords when they forget them. The app is a FastAPI web app with Pydantic models and an in-memory user store. Brainstorm the design, ask whatever clarifying questions you need, then produce the PRD as a standalone document in the workspace. Assume I've answered your questions.
evals.expected_output: The agent conceives the design, then writes a standalone PRD document (not just an in-conversation reply) whose decisions are tied back to numbered user stories with rationale, presenting a coherent design the user can review.
expectations: The PRD is saved as a file in the workspace, not only as a chat reply — a PRD delivered only in the conversation fails this

Every user-story ID an implementation decision names resolves to an entry in the plan's user-story list, and no decision goes without one; a decision citing an ID absent from that list fails this, and so does a decision citing none
Each decision carries a line of rationale — a decision stated with no stated reason fails this
